     2	
     3	Normative. Read `local/protocols/meta.md`, `issues-prs.md`, and `ci.md` first.
     4	
     5	`local/bin/review.sh <github-pr-number>` runs only from a complete CI evidence
     6	set for the current full head and base SHAs. The manifest conclusion must be
     7	`success`, every canonical step must be `success` or `skipped`, and all eight
     8	matching statuses plus the digest-bound `local-ci/summary` must be `success`.
     9	A readable failure or error manifest does not authorize review.
    10	
    11	An ordinary rerun adopts a complete exact-head and exact-base attestation.
    12	`--new-round` explicitly requests another adjudication round for that same
    13	comparison. It changes complete-attestation idempotency and is also the only
    14	way to supersede a canonically aborted pre-attestation attempt. Incomplete
    15	publication of an existing attestation is still finalized without redispatch,
    16	and all comparison, session, CI, bot-commit, and lock guards remain in force.
    17	Repeating the guarded mode can therefore produce the four distinct rounds
    18	required for operator adjudication.
    19	
    20	## Tree and prompt integrity
    21	
    22	After reading the GitHub PR identity, review takes the per-PR review lock and
    23	atomically reserves the same per-branch fix lock used by auto-fix. It holds both
    24	from before its first feature-tree read through review and summary publication.
    25	Both leases carry a PID, random UUID token, directory identity, and a digest of
    26	their complete structured owner metadata. Every ownership check and release is
    27	serialized by the persistent sibling transition mutex. Review aborts if either
    28	exact claim is lost or has a valid cancellation request; malformed owner or
    29	cancellation records also fail closed. Cleanup can remove only the exact claims
    30	acquired by that process, so a whole-directory replacement is preserved.
    31	
    32	The local feature head and fetched local base must equal the GitHub full head
    33	and base SHAs. The feature worktree must have no tracked, staged, or untracked
    34	changes when review starts and immediately before any attestation or final
    35	summary publication, including summary recovery. Provisional pending and
    36	diagnostic error statuses are not review evidence. A moved comparison, dirty
    37	tree, lost lease, or supersession request blocks publication of clean evidence.
    38	
    39	Reviewer personas come from a trusted ref resolved once to a commit. The
    40	reviewed head must not equal that resolved commit, even when the caller used a
    41	different textual spelling for the same ref. Prompt files and dispatcher
    42	persona bindings use the resolved trusted commit, never the feature branch.
    43	
    44	## Reviewer sessions
    45	
    46	Each dispatched lane must have a nonempty session name and thread id distinct
    47	from the other lane, exit zero, and have exactly matching clean completion
    48	telemetry. The matching record binds the reviewer role, PR/issue number,
    49	worktree, thread id, start and end timestamps, and `done` status. Output from a
    50	nonzero reviewer process is diagnostic only and can never satisfy the gate.
    51	
    52	Within one PR, a reviewer session name or thread id may identify only one
    53	distinct attestation. Re-reading or idempotently adopting that same attestation
    54	is allowed; replaying either identity in another head, base, run, or body digest
    55	is rejected before the wrapper posts another review and is invalid evidence. A
    56	run id is likewise owned by one distinct attestation, preventing a same-head
    57	pending status from becoming ambiguous after base movement.
    58	
    59	Reviewer inputs such as diffs, build logs, prior ledgers, issue text, and paper
    60	text are untrusted data. The wrapper strips controls, truncates them, prevents
    61	fence escape, and states that instructions in the data must not be followed.
    62	Before dispatch, it reads and validates the latest marker-bound GitHub ledger
    63	and attaches it with PR metadata so findings carry across heads as explicitly
    64	unresolved, resolved, or outdated. Reviewers cannot publish to GitHub; only the
    65	trusted wrapper does so.
    66	
    67	Lane output remains in runtime storage until combined. The combined body keeps
    68	the findings ledger and path/line references.
    69	
    70	## Output grammar
    71	
    72	Every dispatched review output has exactly one section headed `## Findings`.
    73	Ignoring surrounding blank lines, that section contains either the single line
    74	`- none` or one or more canonical lines of the form:
    75	
    76	```text
    77	- [ ] F1 (changes) `path/to/file:line` — one-line summary
    78	```
    79	
    80	The only checkbox states are `[ ]` (unresolved), `[x]` (resolved), and `[-]`
    81	(outdated); the parser preserves the state instead of reopening resolved or
    82	outdated entries. A location is either a relative ASCII repository path plus a
    83	positive decimal line number or the literal `-`. Finding identifiers, severity,
    84	backticked location, and one-line summary must have the canonical shape. The
    85	verdict trailer occurs exactly once and is the final nonempty line, with one of
    86	the three documented `VERDICT:` values. Missing, duplicate, mixed, or malformed
    87	findings sections, findings lines, or trailers block the run and produce no
    88	clean evidence. Only unresolved entries contribute to the blocking findings
    89	count.
    90	
    91	## Attestation and publication
    92	
    93	Before publication, the wrapper revalidates both leases, worktree cleanliness,
    94	and the local and GitHub full head and base SHAs immediately before each
    95	attestation or final-summary mutation. After its idempotency lookup, the client
    96	repeats the full check around any intervening reviewer-identity or summary-status
    97	read, then finishes with a fast local lease/tree check immediately before the
    98	write. The full authoritative and fast local guards run again after a write
    99	response or authoritative adoption, and after the final evidence readback.
   100	Movement or loss of ownership makes the run stale.
   101	
   102	The wrapper publishes `local-review/summary=pending` under both leases before
   103	dispatch. Pending and pre-attestation diagnostic error descriptions bind a
   104	cryptographic fingerprint of the full current base SHA, the run id, and the
   105	attempt state. The status digest additionally binds the exact head, context,
   106	and GitHub state, and the status creator must be trusted. Every pre-attestation
   107	failure after pending publication, but before the review POST may have started,
   108	attempts the same canonical `error`/`aborted` status. Once review submission may
   109	have started, an ambiguous outcome retains `pending`: it must never be
   110	overwritten with `aborted`, because GitHub may have accepted the attestation.

   112	review with the exact `commit_id`. Clean and adverse reviews alike use
   113	`event=COMMENT` and

   115	attestation binds the full PR number, full head and base SHAs, run id, canonical
   116	findings count, event, and each dispatched review lane's name, thread id, exit,
   117	worktree, and timestamps. Its digest covers the complete canonical ledger body
   118	before the final marker.
   119	
   120	The wrapper separately finalizes `local-review/summary` on that SHA: `success`
   121	only for a zero-finding clean `COMMENT` attestation and `failure` for unresolved
   122	findings. The status description binds the same run and ledger digest.
   123	Publication is idempotent only when the full attestation, digest, body, commit,
   124	event/state, and status agree. Transient and ambiguous review writes use
   125	authoritative read-back and never issue a second review mutation. Transient
   126	reconciliation lookup failures are retried; an unresolved ambiguity is adopted
   127	idempotently on a later rerun if the exact attestation exists.
   128	
   129	The review `COMMENT` row must have `user.login` equal to the configured trusted
   130	actor, and its latest summary must have the same actor in `creator.login`.
   131	Every invocation verifies that the authenticated `gh` user is that actor.
   132	Untrusted or missing-author marker copies are not attestations and cannot
   133	collide with a trusted publication. Summary selection remains global per
   134	context, so a newer untrusted status blocks the gate rather than exposing an
   135	older trusted result. For an otherwise valid latest attestation, the producer
   136	may classify that untrusted or creator-missing summary as recoverable and post
   137	the exact digest-bound trusted final status. A conflicting status from the
   138	trusted actor remains fail-closed.
   139	
   140	A valid review attestation is deliberately distinct from complete merge
   141	evidence. Structural parsing, the exact commit and base, the body digest,
   142	canonical ledger, event semantics, session telemetry, and cross-attestation
   143	session uniqueness can all be validated before a final summary status exists.
   144	Prior-ledger and review-fix consumers may read that valid attestation. Merge
   145	evidence additionally requires the exact matching final summary status.
   146	
   147	If a review POST succeeded but its summary status is missing, remains the
   148	canonical `pending` status for that same attested run, or has been superseded
   149	by an untrusted or creator-missing row, a rerun adopts the existing exact-head,
   150	exact-base attestation without redispatch or a duplicate review POST. After
   151	another full boundary check it idempotently posts the matching trusted final
   152	status and verifies complete evidence. The guarded finalizer reclassifies the
   153	latest summary inside the mutation path, repeats the full authoritative
   154	comparison after that read, and then performs the fast local lease/tree check
   155	before the POST; normal publication uses the same path. A pending status for a
   156	different run, any conflicting trusted status, or an attestation for a stale
   157	base is not recoverable as the current run.
   158	
   159	When there is no corresponding exact-comparison attestation, a trusted
   160	canonical pending or aborted status for the current base is classified as an
   161	aborted attempt only for a caller that explicitly enables `--new-round`
   162	recovery. Ordinary reruns remain fail-closed. A wrong-base attempt, arbitrary
   163	trusted conflict, malformed description, or attempt run already owned by an
   164	attestation is never recoverable through this path. A completed attestation for
   165	an earlier base is historical evidence rather than an aborted attempt and does
   166	not prevent a fresh review after the comparison base advances.
   167	
   168	GitHub approval and `reviewDecision` are never required. The normal gate is a
   169	successful exact-head summary status plus a strictly parsed clean `COMMENT`
   170	attestation whose reviewer session telemetry matches, with no later exact-head
   171	`CHANGES_REQUESTED` review. This supports the common case where the repository
   172	operator is also the PR author and GitHub forbids self-approval.
   173	
   174	An adverse `COMMENTED` attestation remains valid raw ledger evidence for
   175	review-fix consumers, but its summary is `failure` and it never satisfies the
   176	clean merge gate. Raw attestation validation and review-summary merge
   177	eligibility are deliberately separate decisions.
   178	
   179	Kill switches disable only when set to the literal string `false`; unset means
   180	enabled. A reviewer session must be different from every author session and
   181	must never repair its own findings.

1	# Exact-head local CI
     2	
     3	Normative. Read `local/protocols/meta.md` and `issues-prs.md` first.
     4	
     5	Run `local/bin/ci.sh <github-pr-number>`. The command reads the PR base, head
     6	branch, and full head and base SHAs from GitHub through `github_api.py`, resolves
     7	the registered local worktree for that branch, and requires the local head and
     8	trusted local base to match those remote SHAs before work starts. The feature
     9	worktree must also be completely clean: tracked changes, staged changes, and
    10	untracked files all make the run ineligible.
    11	
    12	## Canonical gates
    13	
    14	A complete run evaluates these contexts in order:
    15	
    16	1. `local-ci/build`
    17	2. `local-ci/blueprint-render`
    18	3. `local-ci/paper-gaps`
    19	4. `local-ci/blueprint-sync`
    20	5. `local-ci/file-length`
    21	6. `local-ci/proof-debt`
    22	7. `local-ci/proof-evasion`
    23	8. `local-ci/statement-origin`
    24	
    25	The existing change classifiers and step commands are preserved. Each context
    26	is first `pending`, then `success`, `failure`, or `error`. A non-applicable step
    27	is `success` with a description stating that it was skipped. Context matching
    28	is case-insensitive, because GitHub status contexts are case-insensitive.
    29	
    30	`local-ci/summary` is the required aggregate context, not a ninth executable
    31	step. A complete run publishes it as `pending` before any CI work. Its final
    32	description binds the exact manifest run and canonical JSON digest.
    33	
    34	`--only`, `--skip-build`, and `--dry-run` are diagnostic partial runs. They
    35	write runtime logs but publish no gate-satisfying status set or manifest.
    36	
    37	There are two evidence levels. A complete, exact-head and exact-base manifest
    38	with matching canonical statuses is readable evidence even when its conclusion
    39	is `failure` or `error`; auto-fix uses such evidence to classify a repair. CI
    40	satisfies the review and merge prerequisite only when the manifest conclusion
    41	is `success`, every canonical step outcome is `success` or `skipped`, every
    42	matching step status is `success`, and the latest `local-ci/summary` is the
    43	successful state for that manifest's exact run and digest. Thus a well-formed
    44	failed run remains diagnostic evidence but is never green evidence.
    45	
    46	## Publication
    47	
    48	CI checks cleanliness after binding the initial comparison and again at every
    49	final-publication boundary. Immediately before final statuses and the manifest,
    50	it rereads the local and GitHub head and base SHAs and the complete worktree
    51	status. The shared client repeats this full guard inside each final-status and
    52	manifest mutation, after its idempotency lookup, immediately before the POST,
    53	and after the write response or authoritative adoption. The final manifest and
    54	summary readbacks are guarded again before their evidence is returned.
    55	Movement, an unreadable comparison, or any dirt makes the run stale and returns
    56	nonzero. It publishes no marker-bound manifest; after detecting a
    57	mid-publication change it invalidates that run's contexts with `error`, so the
    58	latest statuses cannot form a successful set. A dirty run therefore cannot
    59	leave gate-satisfying evidence, while a clean, stable failure or error run keeps
    60	its readable manifest for diagnosis and auto-fix.
    61	
    62	A complete stable run posts a full JSON manifest as an immutable PR comment
    63	with exact PR, full head, full base, and run markers. Marker adoption requires
    64	the entire body to match. Every canonical status description names that same
    65	run, and a consumer rejects a manifest unless the latest exact-head status for
    66	every step names the manifest run and agrees with its result. Only after the
    67	comment and all step statuses have been read back authoritatively does CI post
    68	the digest-bound final `local-ci/summary`, then it rereads both the manifest and
    69	summary. A publication failure invalidates the step and summary contexts with
    70	`error`; a prior success can never survive as the latest summary for the failed
    71	run.
    72	
    73	The manifest comment and every step/summary status are authoritative only when
    74	GitHub reports the configured trusted actor as, respectively, `user.login` and
    75	`creator.login`. The actor defaults to the repository owner and is configured
    76	with `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_ACTOR`; `gh api /user` must match before every producer
    77	or consumer invocation. An untrusted copied manifest marker is ignored. Status
    78	rows differ because GitHub resolves required contexts by global latest-row
    79	semantics: the client selects the latest row first, then checks its creator, so
    80	a newer untrusted row fails closed rather than revealing an older trusted
    81	success. A later trusted publication may explicitly supersede it.
    82	
    83	Status creation is digest-idempotent. Each invocation issues at most one
    84	mutation. If the POST result is ambiguous, the client polls statuses on the
    85	exact SHA and adopts only the matching casefolded context, state, and
    86	description digest. Transient reconciliation lookup failures are retried
    87	without issuing a second mutation. It fails ambiguous if read-back does not
    88	establish the mutation and never sends a second POST.
    89	
    90	Logs and manifests are runtime state under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`. Build
    91	events remain append-only in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`. No committed
    92	issue or PR shadow record is created.
    93	
    94	## Build lock
    95	
    96	The per-PR `ci-<number>.lock` is also reserved by the merge gate. Every owner
    97	uses `local/bin/runtime_lock.py` to record a PID, random UUID token, directory
    98	device/inode identity, and structured owner metadata. The metadata repeats the
    99	PID, token, and identity and records the owner label, host, and creation time.
   100	The helper binds a claim to the digest of that complete record.
   101	
   102	Creation, explicit recovery, release, and validation are serialized by `flock`
   103	on the canonical path's persistent sibling transition file. Acquisition never
   104	breaks a complete record, including a dead same-host parent whose descendants
   105	may survive. An explicit recovery or release revalidates the exact identity,
   106	PID, token, and owner digest under that mutex before renaming, then deletes only
   107	the verified private tombstone while still holding the mutex.
   108	
   109	Ownerless, malformed, partial, and foreign-host lock directories are never
   110	removed automatically, regardless of age. They fail closed with the exact path
   111	and require the operator recovery described in `local/README.md`. This prevents
   112	two recovery attempts or an old cleanup handler from moving a replacement
   113	directory.
   114	
   115	Single-file Lean checks do not take the machine-wide lock. Full builds by CI,
   116	the cache warmer, worktree warming, and the housekeeping linter sweep all use
   117	the same helper and `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`, with a worktree-local
   118	copy-on-write cache clone as described by `build-cache.md`. Never run
   119	`lake update`, and never write back to the hot main cache.
   120	
   121	Changes to `local/bin/runtime_lock.py` or `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` are
   122	workflow changes. CI change gating and both installed git hooks must run the
   123	GitHub-native regression suite for either path.
   124	
   125	The merge and review gates require the success-level evidence described above,
   126	bound to the current full head and base SHAs. Classic branch protection also
   127	requires only `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`, with strict base
   128	freshness. GitHub's combined status is not sufficient.

item.text: The review path does enforce success-level CI through the CLI’s `ci-evidence` command, and it never asks GitHub for approval: the only accepted publication event is `COMMENT`, while merge eligibility comes from the separately digest-bound summary. Its recovery path also preserves pending state once a review POST may have begun, which avoids masking an accepted-but-unreadable attestation as aborted. I’m continuing with CI finalization and merge’s last-moment revalidation.

   777	def reserve_runtime_lock(path: Path, label: str) -> Iterator[HeldLock]:
   778	    """Atomically reserve one runtime lock and release only our lease."""
   779	    result = acquire_lock(path, os.getpid(), new_token(), f"pr_merge.py {label}")
   780	    if result.state != "acquired" or result.record is None:
   781	        recovery = ""
   782	        if result.state == "unsafe":
   783	            recovery = (
   784	                "; after verifying no CI, review, auto-fix, or merge process "
   785	                f"owns it, remove {path} explicitly and retry"
   786	            )
   787	        raise GateFailure(
   788	            f"cannot reserve runtime lock {path} "
   789	            f"({result.state}: {result.detail}){recovery}"
   790	        )
   791	    held = HeldLock(path=path, claim=result.record.claim)
   792	    try:
   793	        held.require_owned()
   794	        yield held
   795	    finally:
   796	        try:
   797	            release_owned_lock(held.path, held.claim)
   798	        except (OSError, RuntimeError):

   777	def reserve_runtime_lock(path: Path, label: str) -> Iterator[HeldLock]:
   778	    """Atomically reserve one runtime lock and release only our lease."""
   779	    result = acquire_lock(path, os.getpid(), new_token(), f"pr_merge.py {label}")

   787	        raise GateFailure(

   789	            f"({result.state}: {result.detail}){recovery}"
   790	        )
   791	    held = HeldLock(path=path, claim=result.record.claim)
   792	    try:
   793	        held.require_owned()
   794	        yield held
   795	    finally:
   796	        try:

   163	comparison. Unrelated `ADJUDICATION` prefix prose and untrusted copies are
   164	ignored. The selected row must order strictly after its source review. Its
   165	canonical JSON and final digest marker bind the PR, head, base, and latest
   166	source review id, run, and digest. It cites at least four ordered, distinct,
   167	session-valid review rounds for that same head and base. Its dispositions
   168	exactly cover every unresolved source finding: `fixed` records need nonempty
   169	reason and evidence, while `tracked` records name an open, non-PR issue in the
   170	same repository. After a full revalidation under all three locks, the gate
   171	publishes the exact adjudication as `local-review/summary=success` and rereads
   172	it before merge.
   173	
   174	Because review ids and issue-comment ids come from different namespaces, their
   175	relative values carry no chronology. The source-review/adjudication comparison
   176	uses timestamps only and requires strict inequality; equal timestamps fail
   177	closed regardless of either row's id.
   178	
   179	The only merge mutation is one guarded
   180	`gh pr merge --merge --match-head-commit <sha>` call, without `--admin` or
   181	`--auto`. GitHub's strict required checks and base-freshness rule remain the
   182	server-side last gate. A transient result triggers authoritative PR read-back,
   183	never a second merge call. Read-back retains the frozen head SHA, head ref, and
   184	base ref, but does not require GitHub's post-merge `base.sha` to remain frozen:
   185	GitHub may advance it to the new base tip. Instead, the reported
   186	`merge_commit_sha` must resolve through the Git Data API to exactly two parents,
   187	the frozen base then the frozen head. An already-merged response with different
   188	identity or topology is classified external/nonconforming, not successful
   189	local execution, and receives no cleanup. After topology-verified remote
   190	success, the merge result is final. Fetching and fast-forwarding the trusted
   191	local base and cleaning the feature worktree/branch are separate best-effort
   192	maintenance steps. Dirt such as newly written telemetry or any other local
   193	failure warns and defers that step; it never reports the proven GitHub merge as
   194	failed. Remote identity or topology nonconformance remains fatal and receives
   195	no cleanup.
   196	
   197	Merge reserves the CI, review, and fix runtime directories through the same
   198	helper as their ordinary owners. Each claim contains the directory device/inode
   199	identity, PID, random UUID token, and digest of structured owner metadata. The
   200	persistent sibling `flock` serializes creation, validation, cancellation,
   201	explicit recovery, and release. Under it, any transition based on a prior
   202	observation must match the complete claim before the canonical path is renamed
   203	or a cancellation is written. Cleanup deletes only the verified private
   204	tombstone.
   205	
   206	Acquisition never deletes any existing complete record, including a same-host
   207	dead parent whose descendants may survive. After verifying that the recorded
   208	process and every descendant have stopped, the operator may explicitly break
   209	that exact complete claim through the helper. A directory without a complete
   210	valid owner may be a partial lock or interrupted initializer, so it also is
   211	never deleted automatically, regardless of age. Foreign-host records fail
   212	closed. Manual recovery must target only the exact path from the error after
   213	verifying that no CI, review, auto-fix, agent, merge, or build process owns it.
   214	
   215	## Snapshots and reporting
   216	
   217	`local/bin/github-sync.sh` fetches explicit refs and creates a paginated audit
   218	snapshot. It publishes `open-issues.json`, `open-pulls.json`, and
   219	`metadata.json` as one generation by an atomic symlink switch; a failed
   220	generation leaves the prior one intact. Pull objects are removed from the issue
   221	dataset. `local/bin/housekeeping.sh standup` writes a dated report under
   222	`results/reports/standup/` and never mutates GitHub.
   223	
   224	Every emitted label is validated against GitHub. There is no offline mutation
   225	mode, local sequence allocator, shadow frontmatter, or committed PR manifest.

1	# Build cache protocol — the hot main cache
     2	
     3	Normative. This document specifies the local replacement for the parent
     4	workflow's GitHub Actions build cache, and the rules every worktree must obey to
     5	avoid duplicate compilation. It is the protocol behind three executables:
     6	
     7	| script | role |
     8	|---|---|
     9	| `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh` | the **single writer**: builds `main`, publishes read-only snapshots |
    10	| `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` | the **consumer**: keyhash-gated copy-on-write clone into a worktree |
    11	| `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` | fresh-worktree bootstrap (replaces `.codex/setup.sh`) |
    12	
    13	Governing invariants: `local/DESIGN.md` #1 (single cache writer) and #7 (one full
    14	`lake build` machine-wide). Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,
    15	`DESIGN.md` wins.
    16	
    17	---
    18	
    19	## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way
    20	
    21	The parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented
    22	failure. The load-bearing citations:
    23	
    24	| parent mechanism | citation | what it encodes |
    25	|---|---|---|
    26	| Split restore/save, save only on `main` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:137-167` | *"The cache is saved only from main and restored everywhere."* |
    27	| `lean-action`'s own cache disabled | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:138-142` | The post-mortem: a ~2.6 GB entry saved **per PR run** cycled through the 10 GB repository cache budget and evicted the main-branch entry, *"so no run ever restored usable MIPStarRE oleans and every run rebuilt the whole library."* |
    28	| Same policy restated in the weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget."* |
    29	| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache."* |
    30	| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile."* |
    31	| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |
    32	| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could negate the ProofWidgets workaround"* |
    33	| Independent cache for the doc subproject | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:135-140` | `docbuild/` is its own Lake project with its own key |
    34	| Mathlib bumps are manual only | `.github/workflows/update.yml:3-5` | A bump *"triggers a full library rebuild and possibly an auto-fix cascade"* |
    35	| Lean setup removed from a PR job | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *"after repeated runner disk exhaustion"* |
    36	
    37	The single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable
    38	cache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the
    39	same failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared
    40	build tree.
    41	
    42	---
    43	
    44	## 2. The two-tier split
    45	
    46	`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and
    47	different sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the
    48	parent's failure.
    49	
    50	**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,
    51	`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the
    52	parent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and
    53	distributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**
    54	copy.
    55	
    56	**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The
    57	parent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud
    58	cache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally the same holds:
    59	**every worktree runs its own `lake exe cache get`.**
    60	
    61	> **Tier 2 is never symlinked into a worktree.** A shared `.lake/packages` looks
    62	> attractive (it saves the download), but it is read-only only by convention, and
    63	> a single consumer running `lake update` mutates the tree for every other
    64	> worktree simultaneously. The download is cheap; a corrupted shared dependency
    65	> tree during a multi-agent session is not. `warm-worktree.sh` therefore fetches
    66	> per worktree, and `worktree-setup.sh` refuses to run `lake update` at all.
    67	
    68	Consequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It
    69	rewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under
    70	every published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib
    71	bumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.
    72	
    73	---
    74	
    75	## 3. The cache key
    76	
    77	```
    78	keyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )
    79	```
    80	
    81	concatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local
    82	analog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in
    83	`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`
    84	and `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay
    85	byte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.
    86	A missing input file is a hard error, never a default.
    87	
    88	Two properties matter, and they are not symmetric:
    89	
    90	1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's
    91	   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest
    92	   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is
    93	   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash
    94	   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not
    95	   need their timestamps preserved.
    96	2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,
    97	   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.
    98	   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`
    99	   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls
   100	   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.
   101	
   102	---
   103	
   104	## 4. On-disk layout
   105	
   106	All runtime state lives under `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`, default
   107	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`. Nothing in this tree is ever committed.
   108	
   109	```
   110	~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/
   111	├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time
   112	│   ├── pid                      # positive process id
   113	│   ├── token                    # random UUID4 token
   114	│   ├── identity                 # directory device/inode
   115	│   └── owner                    # structured JSON owner metadata
   116	├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends
   117	├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)
   118	└── hot-main/
   119	    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this
   120	    │   ├── pid
   121	    │   ├── token
   122	    │   ├── identity
   123	    │   └── owner
   124	    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main
   125	    ├── snapshots/
   126	    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
   127	    │   │   ├── STAMP
   128	    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build
   129	    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
   130	    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink
   131	```
   132	
   133	Snapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse
   134	lexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`
   135	calls and no name parsing.
   136	
   137	### `STAMP` schema
   138	
   139	A flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts
   140	parse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase
   141	hex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever
   142	`eval`ed or `source`d.
   143	
   144	```
   145	sha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>
   146	keyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>
   147	timestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>
   148	timestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>
   149	status=complete|partial
   150	build_seconds=<integer>
   151	toolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>
   152	snapshot=<snapshot directory name>
   153	warmer_version=1
   154	```
   155

   158	## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`
   159	
   160	```
   161	local/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]
   162	                          [--targets "<lake targets>"] [--lock-timeout S]
   163	                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]
   164	```
   165	
   166	`--lease-ttl` remains accepted for command-line compatibility. Runtime-lock
   167	staleness is never age-based.
   168	
   169	### 5.1 Writer lease
   170	
   171	The warmer acquires `hot-main/.writer-lease` through
   172	`local/bin/runtime_lock.py`, using the complete claim described in §7. The
   173	helper serializes acquisition and explicit recovery on the lease's persistent
   174	sibling mutex. Acquisition never breaks an existing complete record, even when
   175	its same-host PID is proven dead, because descendants may survive their
   176	recorded parent. A complete dead-owner claim may be broken only by an explicit
   177	recovery operation after the operator has ruled out surviving descendants. A
   178	foreign-host, ownerless, malformed, or partial record fails closed for manual
   179	recovery.
   180	
   181	Explicit recovery renames and removes a dead-owner lease only after
   182	revalidating the exact directory identity and complete owner record under that
   183	mutex. Concurrent recovery attempts therefore serialize, and no observation
   184	made before taking the mutex authorizes a rename.
   185	
   186	### 5.2 Build
   187	
   188	1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`
   189	   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.
   190	   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and
   191	   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).
   192	2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).
   193	3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**
   194	   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and
   195	   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,
   196	   finish, then warm again.
   197	4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply
   198	   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.
   199	   **No `lake update`.**
   200	5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.
   201	   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is
   202	   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent
   203	   prompts may later read.
   204	
   205	### 5.3 Atomic publish
   206	
   207	The publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:
   208	
   209	1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with
   210	   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the
   211	   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).
   212	2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.
   213	3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.
   214	   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already
   215	   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**
   216	4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over
   217	   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).

   226	
   227	### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional
   228	
   229	If `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and
   230	exits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`
   231	commit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did
   232	compile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say
   233	so loudly.
   234	
   235	A non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *"main did not build cleanly"* —
   236	not *"nothing was published."* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a
   237	reason to retry.
   238	
   239	### 5.5 Retention
   240	
   241	Keep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's
   242	10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never
   243	collected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has
   244	resolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging
   245	directories older than an hour are swept.

   248	
   249	## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`
   250	
   251	```
   252	local/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]
   253	                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]
   254	```
   255	
   256	The consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to
   257	operate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.
   258	
   259	Decision procedure:
   260	
   261	1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).
   262	2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.
   263	3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.
   264	4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause
   265	   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the
   266	   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.
   267	5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,
   268	   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker
   269	   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,
   270	   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.
   271	   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that
   272	   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.
   273	6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the
   274	   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.
   275	
   276	### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule
   277	
   278	Re-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:
   279	
   280	* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the
   281	  clone;
   282	* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it
   283	  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it
   284	  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.
   285	
   286	### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink
   287	
   288	On APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near
   289	instantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid
   290	for only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a
   291	*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is
   292	precisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or
   293	bind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations
   294	is the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.
   295	
   296	---
   297	
   298	## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate
   299	
   300	| lock | path | held by | protects |
   301	|---|---|---|---|
   302	| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |
   303	| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |
   304	
   305	They are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the
   306	warmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease
   307	does not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.
   308	
   309	`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They
   310	are read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`
   311	gate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add
   312	locking there.
   313	
   314	The parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that
   315	a CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice
   316	(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale
   317	build; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.
   318	
   319	Both locks use `local/bin/runtime_lock.py`. A complete lease records a PID,
   320	random UUID token, directory device/inode identity, and structured owner
   321	metadata whose digest is part of the immutable claim. Creation, explicit
   322	recovery, owned release, and claim validation are serialized on a persistent
   323	sibling `flock`. Acquisition refuses every complete existing record. A
   324	same-host record with a provably dead PID is eligible only for explicit
   325	recovery after checking for descendants; ownerless, malformed, partial, or
   326	foreign-host records require manual recovery.
   327	
   328	### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`
   329	
   330	`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two
   331	compatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:
   332	
   333	* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,
   334	  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to
   335	  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override
   336	  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the
   337	  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the
   338	  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,
   339	  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see
   340	  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)
   341	* **Metadata layout.** All four takers call the same helper and require the same
   342	  `pid`, `token`, `identity`, and structured JSON `owner` files. The owner JSON
   343	  repeats the first three fields and records the tool label, host, and creation
   344	  time. No participant interprets legacy `info`, age, or directory mtime as
   345	  authority. A complete dead record still blocks acquisition until explicit
   346	  recovery under the transition mutex; any incomplete or inconsistent record
   347	  fails closed with its exact path.
   348	
   349	The warmer's independent writer lease and the best-effort telemetry mutex use
   350	the same ownership primitive. Telemetry retains its five-second fallback to an
   351	unserialized append, but even that fallback never removes an unowned or
   352	replacement mutex directory.
   353	
   354	`cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, and the housekeeping linter sweep map
   355	`INT` and `TERM` to 130 and 143. Their `EXIT` cleanup removes only the private
   356	staging directory and releases only the exact recorded claims; signal cleanup
   357	cannot delete a replacement lease.

   359	---
   360	
   361	## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`
   362	
   363	Replaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s
   364	GitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:
   365	
   366	1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a
   367	   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable
   368	   error.
   369	2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is
   370	   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.
   371	3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only
   372	   if the pin is not already installed.
   373	4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).
   374	5. **`github/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a hard check, because hooks and
   375	   diff-based audits require one coherent fetched comparison base.
   376	6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).
   377	7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the
   378	   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed
   379	   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.
   380	   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).
   381	   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the
   382	   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol
   383	   exists to prevent.
   384	8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`
   385	   calls out `--check` specifically for *"each fresh worktree used for a PR."*
   386	
   387	`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero
   388	if anything is missing.
   389	
   390	### 8.1 Git environment hygiene
   391	
   392	Every invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in
   393	`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every
   394	variable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a
   395	script invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into
   396	Lake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.
   397	
   398	### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround
   399	
   400	Kept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a
   401	pristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.
   402	
   403	*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib
   404	post-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before
   405	fetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not
   406	exist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create
   407	the directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.
   408	
   409	*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is
   410	**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.
   411	Recorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed
   412	by a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts
   413	therefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before
   414	fetching.
   415	
   416	`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete
   417	downloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks
   418	a checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from
   419	source.
   420	
   421	---
   422	
   423	## 9. Telemetry
   424	
   425	Every full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to
   426	`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.
   427	
   428	```jsonc
   429	{"ts": "<ISO 8601 with offset>",
   430	 "kind": "warm" | "rebuild" | "cache-get",
   431	 "trigger": "<who asked for this>",
   432	 "outcome": "success" | "failed",
   433	 "seconds": <int>,
   434	 "sha": "<commit, when known>",
   435	 "note": "<sanitized, ≤400 chars>"}
   436	```
   437	
   438	* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.
   439	* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).
   440	* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.
   441	
   442	Three properties are load-bearing:
   443	
   444	* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked
   445	  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the
   446	  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and
   447	  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.
   448	* **Appends are serialized** through the shared runtime-lock helper, and give up
   449	  after 5 s rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a
   450	  build; every failure path degrades to a warning. The fallback append is
   451	  unserialized but never renames or removes a lock it does not own.
   452	* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400
   453	  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is
   454	  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).
   455

   458	## 10. Operating procedures
   459	
   460	```bash
   461	# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).
   462	local/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main
   463	
   464	# What is published right now?
   465	local/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status
   466	
   467	# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.
   468	local/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis
   469	
   470	# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.
   471	local/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check
   472	
   473	# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.
   474	local/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force
   475	
   476	# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?
   477	local/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status
   478	```
   479	
   480	After a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm
   481	first, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot
   482	is invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run
   483	`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in
   484	each worktree serialized behind one lock.
   485	
   486	---
   487	
   488	## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades
   489	
   490	| condition | behaviour |
   491	|---|---|
   492	| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |
   493	| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |
   494	| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |
   495	| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |
   496	| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Correct, just slower and larger. |
   497	| `lake exe cache get` fails | Warn; tier 2 gets compiled from source. Non-fatal. |
   498	| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |
   499	| Dead same-host owner | Block acquisition; after checking descendants, recover its exact claim explicitly under the transition mutex. |
   500	| Partial/malformed/ownerless/foreign-host lock | Fail closed for manual recovery. |
   501	| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Never a silent no-op. |
   502	| `warm-worktree.sh` missing during bootstrap | Hard error. `--skip-warm` is the explicit opt-out. |
   503	| `github/main` does not resolve | Hard failure naming the explicit fetch needed; gates never silently disable. |
   504	| `python3` absent | Warmer: hard error (needed for the atomic publish). Consumer: warning, telemetry skipped. |

   531	
   532	## 13. Invariant checklist
   533	
   534	A change to any of these scripts must preserve all of the following:
   535	
   536	1. Only `cache-warmer.sh` writes into `hot-main/`. Consumers refuse to run there.
   537	2. `compute_keyhash` is byte-identical across both scripts.
   538	3. A snapshot becomes visible only via `rename(2)`, fully built and stamped.
   539	4. `current` is re-pointed only via `rename(2)` over the symlink — never `mv`.
   540	5. Consumers resolve `current` exactly once per run.
   541	6. Keyhash mismatch → cold path. Never a partial or best-effort reuse.
   542	7. Failed builds still publish, flagged `partial`.
   543	8. GC never removes the snapshot `current` names.
   544	9. At most one full `lake build` machine-wide; `lake env lean` takes no lock.
   545	10. `.lake/packages` is per-worktree and never symlinked; no automated `lake update`.
   546	11. The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround runs before any `lake exe cache get`.
   547	12. Every `lake` / vendored-`git` invocation goes through `run_outside_git_env`.
   548	13. `STAMP` is parsed by whitelist and validated; never `eval`ed or `source`d.
   549	14. Telemetry is best-effort, serialized, sanitized, and lands in the primary checkout.
   550	15. Every degradation is a loud warning or a hard error. Never a silent no-op.

  local result rc=0

    truncated = len(lines) - max_lines
    lines = lines[:max_lines]

    line = line.replace("```", "'''").replace("~~~", "'''")
    if line.startswith("<<<") or line.startswith("# Task"):

sanitize_to() {

    raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()

        keep.append(ch)

# acquire_fix_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
# Per-BRANCH lock WITH supersession: a newer invocation asks the running one to
# stop at a phase boundary (the cancel-in-progress:true analogue of
# auto-fix.yml:259-261).  Reviews use a per-PR lock without cancellation; the
# split is deliberate (auto-fix.yml:29-32).
acquire_fix_lock() {
  local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 holder="" token
  local result rc=0 state identity observed_token digest detail
  local cancel_target="" observed_target cancel_result cancel_rc cancel_state
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
  token="$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/runtime_lock.py" new-token)" || \
    die "cannot allocate a unique runtime-lock token"
  while :; do
    rc=0
    result="$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/runtime_lock.py" acquire \
      "$dir" "$$" "$token" "$label")" || rc=$?
    IFS='|' read -r state identity holder observed_token digest detail <<EOF
$result
EOF
    if [ "$state" = acquired ]; then
      LOCK_HELD="$dir"
      LOCK_IDENTITY="$identity"
      LOCK_PID="$holder"
      LOCK_TOKEN="$observed_token"
      LOCK_DIGEST="$digest"
      [ -z "$detail" ] || warn "$detail at $dir"
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$state" = unsafe ] || [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
      die "unsafe fix lock $dir: ${detail:-helper failure}; recover that exact path manually"
    fi
    observed_target="$identity|$holder|$observed_token|$digest"
    if [ "$state" = busy ] && [ "$cancel_target" != "$observed_target" ]; then
      log "a fix is already running for this branch \
(pid ${holder:-unknown}); requesting supersession"
      cancel_rc=0
      cancel_result="$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/runtime_lock.py" request-cancel \
        "$dir" "$identity" "$holder" "$observed_token" "$digest" \
        "autofix.sh pid=$$ at $(now_utc)" --owner-prefix "autofix ")" || cancel_rc=$?
      IFS='|' read -r cancel_state _ _ _ _ _ <<EOF
$cancel_result
EOF
      if [ "$cancel_state" = unsafe ] || [ "$cancel_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
        die "could not safely request supersession of $dir; manual recovery required"
      fi
      if [ "$cancel_state" = cancel-requested ]; then
        cancel_target="$observed_target"
      elif [ "$cancel_state" = not-cancellable ]; then
        cancel_target="$observed_target"
        log "the branch lock belongs to a non-autofix writer; waiting without cancellation"
      fi
    fi
    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
      die "timed out after ${wait_s}s waiting for the fix lock $dir \
(holder pid ${holder:-unknown}); it did not stop at a phase boundary"
    fi
    sleep 5
    waited=$((waited + 5))
  done
}

# resolve_worktree <branch> — same resolution order as ci.sh: git's own
# worktree registry first, then the .worktrees/<branch> convention.
resolve_worktree() {
  local branch="$1" found="" safe dest have
  found="$(git -C "$ROOT" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
    awk -v b="refs/heads/$branch" '
      /^worktree /{p=substr($0,10)}
      $0 == "branch " b {print p; exit}')"
  if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$found"
    return 0
  fi
  safe="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
  dest="$ROOT/.worktrees/$safe"
  if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
    have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$dest"
      return 0
    fi
    die "$dest exists but is not a worktree of '$branch' (HEAD: ${have:-not a git worktree}); run 'git -C $ROOT worktree prune' or remove it"
  fi
  mkdir -p "$ROOT/.worktrees"
  git -C "$ROOT" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" ||
    die "git worktree add $dest $branch failed"
  if [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" ]; then
    "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" "$dest" >&2 ||
      warn "worktree-setup.sh failed for $dest; the fixer runs without a warmed build cache"
  else
    warn "local/bin/worktree-setup.sh not found; the fix worktree has no warmed Lean build cache (local/protocols/build-cache.md)"
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- lock primitives
# The writer lease and machine-wide build lease use the same helper contract as
# CI and worktree consumers. Ownerless or partial canonical directories stop the
# caller for explicit operator recovery.

acquire_lock() { # <lockdir> <ttl> <timeout-seconds; 0 = forever> <purpose>
  local dir="$1" ttl="$2" timeout="$3" purpose="$4" waited=0 announced=0
  local token result rc=0 state identity holder observed_token digest detail
  : "$ttl"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
  token="$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/runtime_lock.py" new-token)" || return 2
  while :; do
    rc=0
    result="$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/runtime_lock.py" acquire \
      "$dir" "$$" "$token" "cache-warmer.sh $purpose")" || rc=$?
    IFS='|' read -r state identity holder observed_token digest detail <<EOF
$result
EOF
    if [ "$state" = acquired ]; then
      ACQUIRED_LOCK_IDENTITY="$identity"
      ACQUIRED_LOCK_PID="$holder"
      ACQUIRED_LOCK_TOKEN="$observed_token"
      ACQUIRED_LOCK_DIGEST="$digest"
      [ -z "$detail" ] || warn "$detail at $dir"
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$state" = unsafe ] || [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
      warn "unsafe runtime lock $dir: ${detail:-helper failure}; manual recovery required"
      return 2
    fi
    if [ "$announced" -eq 0 ]; then
      log "waiting for the $purpose lock $dir (held by pid=${holder:-unknown})"
      announced=1
    fi
    if [ "$timeout" -ne 0 ] && [ "$waited" -ge "$timeout" ]; then
      return 1
    fi
    sleep 10
    waited=$((waited + 10))
  done
}

release_lock() { # <lockdir> <identity> <pid> <token> <owner-digest>

   521	  [ -d "$tree/.lake/packages" ] || return 0
   522	  # Only tracked modifications are reset.  `git clean` is deliberately NOT run
   523	  # inside a vendored package: it would delete downloaded build output and cost
   524	  # hours to refetch.  If an untracked byproduct still blocks the checkout, the
   525	  # cache fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from source.
   526	  for pkg in "$tree"/.lake/packages/*; do
   527	    [ -d "$pkg/.git" ] || continue
   528	    name="$(basename "$pkg")"
   529	    if [ -n "$(run_outside_git_env git -C "$pkg" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no 2>/dev/null || true)" ]; then
   530	      log "resetting dirty vendored package tree: $name"
   531	      run_outside_git_env git -C "$pkg" reset --hard >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   532	        || warn "could not reset $name; the Mathlib cache fetch may abort"
   533	    fi
   534	  done
   535	  if [ -d "$tree/.lake/packages/proofwidgets" ]; then
   536	    mkdir -p "$tree/.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib"
   537	  fi
   538	}

   542	publish_snapshot() { # <sha> <keyhash> <status> <build-seconds> -> prints the name
   543	  local sha="$1" keyhash="$2" status="$3" seconds="$4" name final
   544	  name="snap-$(stamp_id)-${sha:0:12}"
   545	  final="$SNAPSHOTS/$name"

   547	  mkdir -p "$SNAPSHOTS"
   548	  STAGE_DIR="$SNAPSHOTS/$name.tmp"
   549	  rm -rf "$STAGE_DIR"
   550	  mkdir -p "$STAGE_DIR"
   551	
   552	  cow_copy "$HOT_REPO/.lake/build" "$STAGE_DIR/build"
   553	
   554	  {
   555	    printf 'sha=%s\n' "$sha"
   556	    printf 'keyhash=%s\n' "$keyhash"
   557	    printf 'timestamp=%s\n' "$(iso_now)"
   558	    printf 'timestamp_epoch=%s\n' "$(epoch_now)"
   559	    printf 'status=%s\n' "$status"
   560	    printf 'build_seconds=%s\n' "$seconds"
   561	    printf 'toolchain=%s\n' "$(tr -d '\r\n' < "$HOT_REPO/lean-toolchain")"

   563	    printf 'warmer_version=%s\n' "$WARMER_VERSION"

   567	  mv "$STAGE_DIR" "$final"   # rename(2): a reader never sees a torn snapshot

   576	main() {
   577	  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
   578	    case "$1" in
   579	      --ref)          REF="${2:?--ref needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   580	      --sha)          SHA="${2:?--sha needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   581	      --force)        FORCE=1; shift ;;
   582	      --targets)      EXTRA_TARGETS="${2:?--targets needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   583	      --lock-timeout) LOCK_TIMEOUT="${2:?--lock-timeout needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   584	      --lease-ttl)    LEASE_TTL="${2:?--lease-ttl needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   585	      --keep)         KEEP="${2:?--keep needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   586	      --gc-only)      MODE="gc"; shift ;;
   587	      --status)       MODE="status"; shift ;;
   588	      -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
   589	      *)              usage >&2; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
   590	    esac
   591	  done
   592	
   593	  case "$LOCK_TIMEOUT$LEASE_TTL$KEEP" in
   594	    ''|*[!0-9]*) die "--lock-timeout, --lease-ttl and --keep must be non-negative integers" ;;
   595	  esac
   596	
   597	  mkdir -p "$CACHE_ROOT" "$HOT_MAIN" "$SNAPSHOTS" "$LOG_DIR"
   598	
   599	  if [ "$MODE" = "status" ]; then
   600	    print_status
   601	    return 0
   602	  fi
   603	
   604	  # The writer lease is what makes this the *single* writer (DESIGN.md #1).  It is
   605	  # a separate lock from the full-build lock, so a consumer's incremental build can
   606	  # proceed while the warmer sits idle between commits.
   607	  acquire_lock "$LEASE_DIR" "$LEASE_TTL" 0 "warmer-writer-lease" \
   608	    || die "could not acquire the writer lease at $LEASE_DIR"
   609	  LEASE_IDENTITY="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_IDENTITY"
   610	  LEASE_PID="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_PID"
   611	  LEASE_TOKEN="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_TOKEN"
   612	  LEASE_DIGEST="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_DIGEST"
   613	  LEASE_HELD=1
   614	
   615	  if [ "$MODE" = "gc" ]; then
   616	    gc_snapshots
   617	    return 0
   618	  fi
   619	
   620	  local primary sha keyhash target existing_sha existing_status
   621	  local logfile started elapsed status outcome rc name
   622	
   623	  primary="$(resolve_primary_repo)"
   624	  [ -d "$primary/.git" ] || die "$primary is not a git repository; cannot seed the hot main checkout"
   625	
   626	  ensure_lean_on_path
   627	  sha="$(ensure_hot_repo "$primary" "$REF")"
   628	  keyhash="$(compute_keyhash "$HOT_REPO")"
   629	  log "target sha=$sha keyhash=$keyhash"
   630	
   631	  if [ "$FORCE" -eq 0 ] && target="$(current_target)"; then
   632	    existing_sha="$(stamp_field "$target/STAMP" sha || true)"
   633	    existing_status="$(stamp_field "$target/STAMP" status || true)"
   634	    if [ "$existing_sha" = "$sha" ] \
   635	       && [ "$existing_status" = "complete" ] \
   636	       && [ "$(stamp_field "$target/STAMP" keyhash || true)" = "$keyhash" ]; then
   637	      log "a complete snapshot for $sha is already published; nothing to do (use --force to rebuild)"
   638	      gc_snapshots
   639	      return 0
   640	    fi
   641	  fi
   642	
   643	  # One full `lake build` machine-wide (DESIGN.md #7).  The warmer WAITS instead of
   644	  # aborting, and is never killed for a newer commit: pr-ci.yml:50 — "Do not cancel
   645	  # main-branch runs: they seed the build cache."
   646	  if ! acquire_lock \
   647	      "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK" "$LOCK_TIMEOUT" "$LOCK_TIMEOUT" "full-lake-build"; then
   648	    die "could not acquire the machine-wide full-build lock $FULL_BUILD_LOCK \
   649	within ${LOCK_TIMEOUT}s"
   650	  fi
   651	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_IDENTITY="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_IDENTITY"
   652	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_PID="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_PID"
   653	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_TOKEN="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_TOKEN"
   654	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_DIGEST="$ACQUIRED_LOCK_DIGEST"
   655	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_HELD=1
   656	
   657	  logfile="$LOG_DIR/warm-$(stamp_id)-${sha:0:12}.log"
   658	  started="$(epoch_now)"
   659	  status="partial"
   660	  outcome="failed"
   661	  rc=0
   662	
   663	  log "building $sha in $HOT_REPO (log: $logfile)"
   664	  seed_hot_repo_lake "$primary"
   665	  proofwidgets_fresh_state_workaround "$HOT_REPO"
   666	  printf '=== cache-warmer %s sha=%s keyhash=%s ===\n' "$(iso_now)" "$sha" "$keyhash" > "$logfile"
   667	
   668	  # No `lake update` here.  `lake exe cache get` fetches Mathlib oleans into
   669	  # .lake/packages; `lake update` would move lake-manifest.json out from under the
   670	  # keyhash and mutate the vendored package trees (two-tier split, see
   671	  # local/protocols/build-cache.md).
   672	  if ! ( cd "$HOT_REPO" && run_outside_git_env lake exe cache get ) >> "$logfile" 2>&1; then
   673	    warn "lake exe cache get failed; continuing to build from source (see $logfile)"
   674	  fi
   675	
   676	  if ( cd "$HOT_REPO" && run_outside_git_env lake build ) >> "$logfile" 2>&1; then
   677	    status="complete"
   678	    outcome="success"
   679	  else
   680	    rc=1
   681	    # pr-ci.yml:161-162 — "Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still
   682	    # spares the next run the modules that did compile."
   683	    warn "lake build failed; publishing a PARTIAL snapshot (see $logfile)"
   684	  fi
   685	
   686	  if [ "$status" = "complete" ] && [ -n "$EXTRA_TARGETS" ]; then
   687	    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
   688	    if ! ( cd "$HOT_REPO" && run_outside_git_env lake build $EXTRA_TARGETS ) >> "$logfile" 2>&1; then
   689	      status="partial"
   690	      outcome="failed"
   691	      rc=1
   692	      warn "extra targets ($EXTRA_TARGETS) failed; the snapshot is flagged partial"
   693	    fi
   694	  fi
   695	
   696	  elapsed=$(( $(epoch_now) - started ))
   697	
   698	  release_lock "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK" "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK_IDENTITY" \
   699	    "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK_PID" "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK_TOKEN" "$FULL_BUILD_LOCK_DIGEST"
   700	  FULL_BUILD_LOCK_HELD=0
   701	
   702	  if [ ! -d "$HOT_REPO/.lake/build" ]; then
   703	    append_build_telemetry "warm" "failed" "$elapsed" "cache-warmer ref=$REF" "$sha" \
   704	      "no .lake/build produced; nothing published; log=$logfile"
   705	    die "no .lake/build directory was produced; nothing to publish (see $logfile)"
   706	  fi
   707	
   708	  name="$(publish_snapshot "$sha" "$keyhash" "$status" "$elapsed")"
   709	  log "published $name (status=$status, ${elapsed}s); current -> $SNAPSHOTS/$name"
   710	
   711	  gc_snapshots
   712	  append_build_telemetry "warm" "$outcome" "$elapsed" "cache-warmer ref=$REF" "$sha" \
   713	    "snapshot=$name status=$status keyhash=$keyhash log=$logfile"
   714	
   715	  return "$rc"
   716	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# dispatch.sh — the only sanctioned way to start a codex agent session.
     3	#
     4	# Usage:
     5	#   local/bin/dispatch.sh --role <orc|prover|reviewer|simplifier|blueprint|splitter|scout>
     6	#                         --issue <id|scope>
     7	#                         [--worktree DIR]        working root (default: repo root)
     8	#                         [--sandbox MODE]        read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access
     9	#                         [--persona FILE]        repo-relative => read from the trusted ref
    10	#                         [--persona-ref REF]     trusted ref for personas (default: main)
    11	#                         [--no-persona]          dispatch with the built-in role frame only
    12	#                         [--resume THREAD_ID]    continue an existing codex thread
    13	#                         [--effort LEVEL]        model_reasoning_effort override
    14	#                         [--context-file FILE]   untrusted data to attach (repeatable)
    15	#                         [--pr ID]               PR id recorded in the registry line
    16	#                         [--skip-hook-check]     do not install/verify git hooks
    17	#                         [--lock-wait SECONDS]   wait for a busy worktree (default 0)
    18	#                         [--dry-run]             print the composed prompt and exit
    19	#                         -- "task prompt"
    20	#
    21	# Replaces the parent repository's GitHub-hosted agent entry points: the
    22	# @claude/@codex mention responder (.github/workflows/claude.yml) and the
    23	# agent invocations inside pr-review.yml / auto-fix.yml, whose bot identity,
    24	# trusted-prompt checkout and run accounting came from GitHub. Locally the
    25	# equivalents are: this script's single entry point (identity), `git show
    26	# <ref>:<path>` for personas (trusted prompts, DESIGN.md invariant 5), and
    27	# results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl (accounting, DESIGN.md "Agent sessions").
    28	#
    29	# What it does, in order:
    30	#   1. validates the role, sanitizes the scope (bracket-free naming),
    31	#      resolves the sandbox default, honours LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED;
    32	#   2. allocates a session name <role>-<scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq> under a lock;
    33	#   3. installs/verifies the per-worktree git hooks for write sessions;
    34	#   4. composes the prompt: persona (from the trusted ref) + session context
    35	#      + sanitized untrusted attachments + the task;
    36	#   5. runs `codex exec --json -C <worktree> --sandbox <mode> </dev/null`,
    37	#      teeing the event stream to results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl;
    38	#   6. appends the registry line via local/bin/telemetry.py and prints
    39	#      name, thread_id and the last-message path.
    40	#
    41	# Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage · 3 disabled by kill switch · 4 preflight failure
    42	#   · 5 worktree busy · 6 telemetry failure · otherwise codex's own status.
    43	#
    44	# Environment: MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT (runtime state root, default
    45	#   ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev), MIPSTARRE_PERSONA_REF, MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL,
    46	#   MIPSTARRE_SESSION (dispatching session name), MIPSTARRE_DISPATCH_LOCK_WAIT,
    47	#   MIPSTARRE_MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES, LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED.
    48	
    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	
    51	PROG="${0##*/}"
    52	
    53	ROLES="orc prover reviewer simplifier blueprint splitter scout"
    54	READ_ONLY_ROLES="reviewer scout"
    55	
    56	# Prompt-size guards. The study fleet lost a session to an oversized prompt
    57	# (results/telemetry/events.md, 2026-08-30 "Workflow critic stalled on
    58	# oversized prompt"); fail loudly rather than hang a paid session.
    59	PROMPT_WARN_BYTES=65536
    60	PROMPT_MAX_BYTES=262144
    61	MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES="${MIPSTARRE_MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES:-20000}"
    62	
    63	die() {
    64	  local code="$1"
    65	  shift
    66	  printf '%s: error: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2
    67	  exit "$code"
    68	}
    69	
    70	note() {
    71	  printf '%s: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2
    72	}
    73	
    74	usage() {
    75	  # Print the header comment block (everything from line 2 up to the first
    76	  # non-comment line) as the help text.
    77	  awk 'NR > 1 && /^#/ { sub(/^# ?/, ""); print; next } NR > 1 { exit }' "$0"
    78	}
    79	
    80	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    81	# Locking (runtime_lock.py owns every directory transition)
    82	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    83	
    84	LOCK_DIRS=()
    85	LOCK_IDENTITIES=()
    86	LOCK_PIDS=()
    87	LOCK_TOKENS=()
    88	LOCK_DIGESTS=()
    89	
    90	release_locks() {
    91	  local index
    92	  for ((index = 0; index < ${#LOCK_DIRS[@]}; index++)); do
    93	    python3 "$RUNTIME_LOCK" release-owned \
    94	      "${LOCK_DIRS[$index]}" "${LOCK_IDENTITIES[$index]}" \
    95	      "${LOCK_PIDS[$index]}" "${LOCK_TOKENS[$index]}" \
    96	      "${LOCK_DIGESTS[$index]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    97	  done
    98	  LOCK_DIRS=()
    99	  LOCK_IDENTITIES=()
   100	  LOCK_PIDS=()
   101	  LOCK_TOKENS=()
   102	  LOCK_DIGESTS=()
   103	}
   104	
   105	cleanup() {
   106	  release_locks
   107	  # A capture file is created early to reserve the sequence number. If we die
   108	  # before codex ever ran, release it again so the number is not burned and no
   109	  # empty "session" is left behind for the archivist to explain.
   110	  if [ "${CODEX_STARTED:-0}" -eq 0 ] \
   111	    && [ -n "${CAPTURE:-}" ] && [ -f "${CAPTURE:-}" ] && [ ! -s "${CAPTURE:-}" ]; then
   112	    rm -f "$CAPTURE"
   113	  fi
   114	  if [ -n "${RUN_TMPDIR:-}" ] && [ -d "${RUN_TMPDIR:-}" ]; then
   115	    rm -rf "$RUN_TMPDIR"
   116	  fi
   117	}
   118	
   119	acquire_lock() {
   120	  # acquire_lock <name> <wait-seconds> <purpose>
   121	  local name="$1" wait_s="$2" purpose="$3"
   122	  local dir="$LOCK_DIR/$name.lock"
   123	  local waited=0 token result rc state identity owner observed_token digest detail
   124	  mkdir -p "$LOCK_DIR"
   125	  token="$(python3 "$RUNTIME_LOCK" new-token)" || \
   126	    die 5 "cannot allocate a runtime-lock token for $purpose"
   127	  while :; do
   128	    rc=0
   129	    result="$(python3 "$RUNTIME_LOCK" acquire \
   130	      "$dir" "$$" "$token" "dispatch.sh $purpose")" || rc=$?
   131	    IFS='|' read -r state identity owner observed_token digest detail <<EOF
   132	$result
   133	EOF
   134	    if [ "$state" = acquired ]; then
   135	      LOCK_DIRS[${#LOCK_DIRS[@]}]="$dir"
   136	      LOCK_IDENTITIES[${#LOCK_IDENTITIES[@]}]="$identity"
   137	      LOCK_PIDS[${#LOCK_PIDS[@]}]="$owner"
   138	      LOCK_TOKENS[${#LOCK_TOKENS[@]}]="$observed_token"
   139	      LOCK_DIGESTS[${#LOCK_DIGESTS[@]}]="$digest"
   140	      return 0
   141	    fi
   142	    if [ "$state" = unsafe ] || [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
   143	      die 5 "$purpose has an unsafe runtime lock ($dir: ${detail:-unknown}).
   144	  Recover that exact path explicitly; no dispatcher may delete it automatically."
   145	    fi
   146	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   147	      die 5 "$purpose is locked by pid ${owner:-unknown} ($dir).
   148	  Another dispatch is writing there. Wait, or pass --lock-wait SECONDS.
   149	  Only one writing session per worktree (DESIGN.md invariant 1, single writer).
   150	  Complete dead-owner records also require explicit recovery because descendants may survive."
   151	    fi
   152	    sleep 2
   153	    waited=$((waited + 2))
   154	  done
   155	}

   158	trap 'exit 130' INT

item.text: One cancellation edge needs closer scrutiny: a newer autofix can mark the current lease while its agent is editing but before the wrapper has created a commit. The wrapper’s next lease assertion appears to abort immediately, potentially leaving the worktree dirty and preventing the replacement run from acquiring usable state. I’m checking the protocol and tests to determine whether that is intentional recovery behavior or a merge blocker.
